MULTISTAGE AMPLIFIER TROUBLESHOOTING PRACTICE
OBJECTIVES
w Identify faulty multistage amplifier operation.
w Determine the faulty component in a faulted multistage amplifier......
. The experiment in this lesson is not setup to use the selected trainer.
EQUIPMENT REQUIRED
Nida Experiment Card PC130 - 33
Nida Experiment Card PC130 - 34
In this lesson, you will determine if a multistage amplifier circuit is faulted and if so, what the fault is.
INTRODUCTIONM
Measuring input and output signals, and comparing measured with calculated values determines if a multistage amplifier is operating correctly.
Signal tracing locates the fault to a specific stage in the amplifier.
Measuring DC operating voltages on the transistor indicates possible component faults.
Resistance measurements confirm a suspected component failure.
Let's begin the lesson on MULTISTAGE AMPLIFIER TROUBLESHOOTING PRACTICE.....

. The experiment in this lesson is not setup to use the selected trainer.
MULTISTAGE AMP TS PRACTICE

The purpose of this experiment is to give you practice in determining if a multistage amplifier circuit is operating normally. If the circuit is faulted you will determine the faulty stage and find the faulty component.
EXPERIMENT
The multistage amplifier circuit is made up of two cards,
PC130-33 contains the first and second stage.
It consists of two common emitter class A RC coupled amplifiers. Q1 is stage 1 and Q2 is stage 2.
The input is from a function generator and the output is fed to stage 3.
PC130-34 contains the third and fourth stage...............
It consists of a driver amplifier and a push-pull amplifier. Q1 is stage 3, Q2 and Q3 are stage 4.
The input is from stage 2 and the output is connected to a speaker. Let's start the experiment.
